column1: Tab 15 — Sign-up, sign-in, profile (Me) and Help/SOS lines

column3: Rule in plain words
No browse mode. Without an account a person can see Welcome, How FigCit works, Help/SOS, Privacy, Terms, Create account and Sign in. Check-in and tools need an account.
column4: Removes the dead ends seen in testing; the age rule and data protection need an account.

column3: Create an account with: email and password; email one-time code (link plus 6-digit code); Continue with Google. A method that is not configured is hidden, never shown as an error.
Only four: 'What should we call you?' (name or nickname, 1–30 characters, any script, editable later); email; age band; country (UK nation if in the UK). Plus acceptance of Terms and Privacy.
column4: Data minimisation (UK GDPR). Sex, full date of birth, diagnosis, profession and study level are NOT asked at sign-up.

column3: Ask 'How old are you?' — 18 or over / 16 or 17 / Under 16. 18+: continue. 16–17: join through a college or university (institution code or institution sign-in); without one, explain kindly and show Help/SOS. Under 16: FigCit isn't available yet; show Help/SOS and Childline 0800 1111. Store only the age band, never a date of birth.
column4: One UK-wide rule, including Scottish 16–17-year-olds at college or university.

column3: Pick a country; if United Kingdom, pick England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland. Used only for Help/SOS numbers, legal notices and service availability.
column4: Help/SOS must show the right lines (Tab 15 HELP rows).

column3: Pre-fill 'What should we call you?' with the Google first name (editable) and the email; then ask age band and country before the account is active.
column4: Google never supplies age or country.

column3: Code or link valid 10 minutes; Resend after 60 seconds; 'Check your spam folder' hint; sent from an @figcit.co.uk address with SPF, DKIM and DMARC set.
column4: The test sign-in email did not appear in the inbox.

column3: Terms and Privacy acceptance required; product-update emails optional and unticked; research consent asked later in Me, never at sign-up.
After sign-up: 'Hello, {name}' → one optional comfort screen (text size, theme, low stimulation; Skip) → first check-in or Home.
Plain, blame-free messages with one next step; never raw JSON, codes or stack traces.
Rule in plain words
Sign in with email and password, email one-time code, or Google (and institution sign-in where licensed). 'Remember this device' optional.
Calm message; try again or reset; lock briefly after the configured number of failures; never reveal whether an email has an account.
Time-limited link; set a new password; other sessions signed out.
Apply comfort settings before the first screen; restore support plan, practices, reminders, plan and last state.
Home greets by the saved name: 'Good morning, {name}'. Never 'you' as a stand-in for a name.
Shown only when signed in. Confirms once, saves unsynced data. 'Sign out of all devices' in Settings.
Admin and institution roles must use multi-factor authentication.
Rule in plain words

A dismissible Home card 'Make FigCit more yours (optional)' appears after the first completed check-in. If dismissed, it may return after 7 days, at most 3 times. Never shown in Amber, Red, Blue or after a safety event.

Pronouns; what fills most of your week (studying, working, looking for work, training or apprenticeship, caring, other); study level; job or field; help or devices I often carry (shown first as UNSELECTED chips on Where you are — never pre-ticked, CTX-0).

Heading 'Life right now'. Question: 'Is anything big going on for you right now?' Options: Losing someone or something (bereavement, break-up); A big change (moving home, new job, course or role); Money pressures; Work or study pressure; Left or between a job, course or training; Caring for someone; Feeling alone; Feeling stuck; Being treated unfairly; Prefer not to say. Multi-select, editable, deletable. No clinical or harm options: abuse, neglect, accident or injury, physical health and mental health are not asked.

Never changes the colour (LE-0). Used for: a validating line on the card, the order of support cards (e.g. losing someone → Reflect, Connect, Meditate first) and signposting. Never shown to organisations; never used to choose faith content.

A fixed line always shown under the list: 'If someone is hurting you or you don't feel safe, tap Help.' Tapping opens Help/SOS with the nation's lines (SF-3). Nothing about it is stored. Free text anywhere still passes the safety check (SF-1).

Life right now holds no health or harm categories and 'Being treated unfairly' does not name a reason, so it is not special category data. It is still private by default, excluded from organisation views and analytics unless the user opts in, and editable or deletable at any time.

Messages to trusted contacts are sent from the user's own phone (SMS, call or their messaging app), outside FigCit. FigCit only prepares the words and opens the phone's own app; it does not carry user-to-user messages.
There is no peer community or user-to-user feature in FigCit.

column3: Rule in plain words
A short, skippable 'Set things up your way' sheet appears BEFORE the first check-in.
Colour theme (Light, Dark, Soft colours, High contrast); language; text size; reduced motion; voice guidance on/off; sounds and vibration; check-in reminders.
Settings icon on Home at all times; changes apply straight away.
All accessibility settings are free (text size, contrast, reduced motion, voice). Extra decorative themes are Prime.
English at launch; the language list is configuration. Help/SOS lines stay in English with the nation's numbers until translated and checked.

column1: v5.0 — Return to work, study or training; FIT advocacy

column3: Rule in plain words
Me → 'What fills most of your week' gains 'Getting back to work, study or training'. Turning it on adds the day's load check (TK-6) and the tools below.
Each morning (or before a shift or class): a Quick check-in, then 'Today fits: …' using the chips, e.g. Amber → 'the usual things and one can't-wait'.

column2: Before a shift, class, interview or appointment
column3: 30–60 min before (timeline T0–T2): a 2-minute settle, a checklist, and 'Notes for my appointment' (Express) for Jobcentre, GP or review meetings.
Express template that turns the user's own words (and, in Premium, their patterns) into a short adjustment request. Never sends automatically; the user copies or shares it from their phone.

2–4 weeks of check-ins shown as capacity against the chips the user worked on: which kinds of task fitted which colours. Owned by the user; shared only if they choose. Links to a Capacity Fit Profile.
Organisation seats see only anonymised group trends (minimum group size applies); never an individual's check-ins, feelings or summary.
